methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atomic Semi is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Sam Zeloof and Jim Keller, having raised $15M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a broader comp universe of 11 private and 3 public companies in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including peers such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched, alongside public comparables including Nvidia, AMD, and Asanko Gold.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised of $15M as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier to approximate next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $38M. This reflects typical dilution and value creation expectations between seed and Series A financings in semiconductor development.

A peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient depth in the narrow peer set—while 11 same-sector comparables exist, fewer than 3 peers meet same-stage or adjacent-stage filters with comparable valuation tier, making broad-sector medians misleading. The analysis therefore relies on stage-progression methodology alone. The single-method constraint yields a valuation range of $32M to $43M, centered at $38M. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct same-stage peer validation and the dependence on capital-raised proxy. Additional clarity on near-term funding milestones and technical differentiation would strengthen conviction in this range.
